principle_text: When the persuadee is open to discussing donation amounts but has not settled on a figure, you should propose a specific amount to facilitate concrete negotiation and advance the conversation.
When the persuadee expresses uncertainty about an agreed donation amount, avoid simply agreeing without reinforcing the value or impact of the contribution.
When the persuadee expresses uncertainty about donation amounts, avoid making general statements that do not directly address their concerns or guide them toward a specific contribution.

When the persuadee expresses concern that a donation amount may be too high, you should acknowledge their concern while emphasizing the positive impact of a larger contribution to encourage agreement.
When the persuadee expresses agreement with a proposed donation amount, you should affirm their choice to build consensus and encourage further engagement about the impact of their contribution.
When the persuadee seeks specific information about the impact of their donation, avoid giving vague or unclear responses that fail to clarify how their contribution helps.
When the persuadee expresses hope or uncertainty about the impact of a donation amount, you should specify a concrete, positive outcome to reinforce the value and encourage agreement.
When the persuadee expresses acceptance of a proposed donation amount, avoid simply confirming agreement without reinforcing commitment or enthusiasm to encourage stronger donation intent.
